value.overview: The Thick-billed Seed-Finch (Sporophila funerea) is a small, heavy-billed songbird of tropical Central America and the Chocó region of northwestern South America. It is associated mainly with grassy, brushy, and lightly wooded habitats rather than deep forest. Adult males are mostly black with a small white wing patch, while females and immature birds are rich brown. Its exceptionally stout bill is an important feature for identifying it among similar seedeaters.
value.classification: The Thick-billed Seed-Finch belongs to the tanager family, Thraupidae, and the seedeater genus Sporophila. It was formerly placed in the genus Oryzoborus.
value.identification: This compact finch has a very thick, deep bill suited to cracking hard seeds. The adult male is nearly all black, with a small white patch on the wing and sometimes subtle variation in plumage depending on wear or molt. The female is uniformly warm brown, and immature birds resemble females. The large bill and relatively straight upper bill profile help separate it from the similar Variable Seedeater and other Sporophila species. It is usually encountered alone or in pairs.
value.rangeHabitat: The species ranges from southern Mexico through Central America to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador. In Costa Rica it is a resident species, occurring mainly in lowlands and foothills on the Caribbean slope and in the southern Pacific region. It generally occurs up to about 1,100 meters, with occasional records higher. Typical habitats include humid grasslands, pastures, abandoned fields, brushy clearings, forest edges, and other areas with scattered shrubs and small trees.
value.migrationStatus: Resident in Costa Rica and across most of its range. It is not considered a regular long-distance migrant, although local movements may occur when food or habitat conditions change.
value.breeding: Breeding occurs in suitable lowland and foothill habitats, where pairs use shrubby vegetation, field edges, and woodland margins. The nest is a small cup made from plant fibers and other fine materials, usually placed in a shrub or low tree. The female generally performs most nest construction and incubation, while both adults may feed the young. Exact details of clutch size, nesting season, and parental roles can vary geographically and are not equally well documented throughout the range.
value.dietFeeding: The Thick-billed Seed-Finch feeds mainly on seeds, especially those of grasses and other herbaceous plants. Its powerful bill allows it to handle relatively large or hard seeds. It typically forages in grass, weeds, and low vegetation, sometimes perching on stems while removing or eating seeds. Insects and other small invertebrates may be taken occasionally, particularly when feeding nestlings or when seeds are less available.
value.behavior: This species is often secretive despite using open habitats. It is commonly seen singly or in pairs rather than in large mixed flocks. Individuals move through grasses, shrubs, and field edges while searching for seeds, and they may remain still for long periods before making a short flight to another perch. Males have a distinctive song used in territorial and courtship contexts, and pairs defend breeding areas during the nesting season.

conservation.populationTrend: Stable overall, although detailed population estimates are limited.
